question: Two long solenoids have the same length. Solenoid A has $1200$ turns and carries a current of $1.5\text{ A}$, while solenoid B has $800$ turns and carries a current of $3.0\text{ A}$. Using the expression for magnetic field inside a long solenoid, compare the magnetic fields inside the two solenoids and justify which one produces the stronger field.

options.A: For equal lengths, $B\propto N/I$. Thus, $\dfrac{B_B}{B_A}=\dfrac{800/3.0}{1200/1.5}=\dfrac13$, so A is stronger.
options.B: For equal lengths, $B\propto N+I$. Thus, $B_A:B_B=1201.5:803.0$, so A is stronger.
options.C: For equal lengths, $B\propto N/I$. Thus, $\dfrac{B_B}{B_A}=\dfrac43$, so B is stronger.
options.D: Since $B=\mu_0(N/l)I$, for the same length $B\propto NI$. Thus, $N_AI_A=1200(1.5)=1800$ and $N_BI_B=800(3.0)=2400$, giving $\dfrac{B_B}{B_A}=\dfrac{2400}{1800}=\dfrac43$. Therefore, solenoid B produces the stronger field.
